metadata.title: Variables Derived from the Student and Teacher Questionnaires – Populations 1 and 2 (Supplement 4) Primary and Middle School Years – 1995 Assessment User Guide for the TIMSS International Database

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This supplement is documentation for derived variables in the TIMSS International Database rather than an empirical analysis paper. It describes how derived contextual variables are computed from TIMSS student and teacher background questionnaire items for Populations 1 and 2, including general analysis rules and country-specific exclusions/adaptations. Because no student-level modeling or estimation is performed here, the document does not specify whether analysts should apply complex survey weights or which weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to use. For secondary analyses using TIMSS microdata, users should follow the TIMSS International Database user guide guidance on complex survey design and apply the appropriate sampling/replicate weights when producing population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values; it only provides variable derivation documentation for contextual questionnaire-based reporting variables. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the supplement’s purpose. Missing-data handling is not reported because the supplement focuses on the computation rules and national exclusion/adaptation documentation for derived variables, not on an estimation procedure with an explicit missing-data strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used for documentation of derived variables in the TIMSS International Database; no analytic sample is defined in this supplement. The document instead specifies that some countries are excluded from particular derived variables (Code X) or included with documentation (Code D) due to missing or unavailable source questionnaire variables or other report-related exclusions.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS International Database supplement documents how derived contextual variables are created from student and teacher background questionnaires for Populations 1 and 2. It explains that Population 1 uses a single student questionnaire version and that derived variables based on general, mathematics-related, and science-related background questions are computed for all students; teacher-derived variables are also generally included for all teachers, with subject-specific handling when separate mathematics and science teachers exist. For Population 2, derived variables depend on whether countries administered specialized versus non-specialized science questionnaire versions, leading to different sets of derived variables for integrated science versus separate science subject areas (biology, chemistry, earth science, physics). The supplement also provides analysis notes for computation rules and tables indicating national exclusions/adaptations (Code X vs Code D) when source items are unavailable or national adaptations modify interpretation. No predictive modeling results or performance metrics are reported because the document is variable documentation rather than an empirical study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a TIMSS user guide supplement focused on documentation of derived questionnaire variables, not an empirical study with an analytic sample, model training, or reported predictive performance. Consequently, fields such as total sample size, country-level Ns, plausible-value handling, missing-data handling strategy for estimation, and ML techniques are not applicable or not reported within the document’s scope. The supplement’s value is methodological transparency for secondary analyses, especially regarding how national questionnaire adaptations and exclusions affect derived variable availability and interpretation.
